title: Getting Started
summary: Sign in, navigate with D-pad, press X to select, and use O to go back.

title: Controller Guide
summary: PS/Home toggles the modal Dashboard tab selector from every Dashboard-owned surface, including Legacy. While it is open, Up/Down move only its highlight, X activates, and Circle or PS/Home closes it. Hold Start opens System Overview Manager • Circle x5 returns once to the configured Home Dashboard Tab • Triangle details • Square actions • L1/R1 sections.

title: Dashboard
summary: PS/Home opens and closes System Overview, Security, Storage, Apps, Legacy and custom tabs. Hold Start manages widget availability, size, movement, defaults, and custom tabs. Running Apps > Square > Make App a Tab reuses the running lifecycle. Apps uses poster artwork with dynamic name plates. Focus uses a luminous couch-distance treatment.

title: Applications
summary: Open Apps, choose a tile, and press X. Running Apps keeps background sessions visible. Docker is available through Apps or Services.

title: Settings
summary: Settings groups System, Display, Audio, Bluetooth, Network, Security, Notifications, Recovery, Controller, Applications, and Developer controls.

title: Networking
summary: Open Network, choose Wi-Fi, scan, select an SSID, and enter its password with the virtual keyboard. Diagnostics never change the active route.

title: Bluetooth
summary: Open Bluetooth, scan, choose a device, then X to pair/connect. Triangle shows battery, signal, trust, and device details.

title: Audio
summary: Open Audio, select HDMI, USB DAC, or Bluetooth output, then adjust volume. Use Test Left, Test Right, or Test Stereo.

title: Storage
summary: Storage Manager shows mounted drives and low-space warnings. Backups can target a mounted USB or external drive.

title: Security
summary: Security Overview shows the Unified Security Core. Profiles map to DEFCON; MAXIMUM keeps the existing double-arm requirement.

title: Updates
summary: Check, download, signature-verify, and stage a release. VERIFIED appears only after the trusted manifest and artifact hash pass.

title: Recovery
summary: Developer Mode exposes one-shot Recovery in Power. The next boot is a local terminal; reboot from Recovery returns to normal.

title: Notifications
summary: Open Notification Center for persistent grouped history. Read state is retained. Security-critical alerts bypass Do Not Disturb.

title: Troubleshooting
summary: Run System Diagnostics, inspect evidence, open Logs, check failed Services, and reboot only after preserving useful evidence.

title: Keyboard
summary: Text fields open the local virtual keyboard. D-pad navigates, X types, Square changes layout where available, and O closes.

title: Developer Mode
summary: Developer Mode unlocks Recovery and advanced controls. It does not bypass authorization, protected-service policy, or update signatures.

title: Create a Backup
summary: Open Recovery > Backups, select settings, profiles, layouts, app configuration, and optional app data, then choose a mounted destination and Create.

title: Safe Mode
summary: After three genuine startup failures NeutronOS stops the GUI loop and opens a tty. Inspect journalctl -b -u neutronos.service, repair, then reboot.

title: DEFCON and Profiles
summary: NORMAL through MAXIMUM are human-friendly policy sets above the existing DEFCON engine; they do not create a second security engine.
